recall_prompt: Say how you would find the square root of a complex number — what you compute first and what formula you put it into.
insider_note: The formula's sign choice needs a sentence: b = 24 is positive, so the two parts of the root take the same sign, giving ±(4 + 3i). Keep the ± — a square root has two values — and the one-line check by squaring catches any swap of the 16 and the 9.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find the modulus
steps.margin_note: First mark. Read off a = 7, b = 24 and find r = √(a² + b²). Here 7, 24, 25 is a Pythagorean triple, so r = 25.

recall.must_convey: That a = 7, b = 24 and the modulus r = √(49 + 576) = 25.
accept: a is seven, b is twenty four, and r is root of forty nine plus five seventy six which is twenty five

modulus kanukunte root six twenty five, twenty five vasthundi

steps.why: The square-root formula is written in terms of r and a. r is the only new number to compute, and it must be a whole number here because the question is built on the 7-24-25 triple.

steps.label: Apply the formula
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Since b > 0 the two parts have the same sign. (25 + 7)/2 = 16 and (25 − 7)/2 = 9 — both perfect squares, which is the check that the arithmetic is right.

recall.must_convey: That the formula √(a + ib) = ±(√((r + a)/2) + i√((r − a)/2)) gives ±(√16 + i√9) = ±(4 + 3i).
accept: use root of r plus a by two plus i root of r minus a by two, that is root sixteen plus i root nine, so plus or minus four plus three i
the square root is plus or minus four plus three i

steps.why: Every non-zero complex number has two square roots, one the negative of the other — that is the ±. When b is positive both parts of the root share a sign; when b is negative they have opposite signs (see the next question).
common_mistakes: Swapping (r + a)/2 and (r − a)/2 to get ±(3 + 4i), which squares to −7 + 24i.
Not checking by squaring — the check takes one line and catches every sign error.
